subject: Re: MAP cost probe — token economics & batching/caching assumptions
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@stratoshealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratoshealth.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — baseline cost assumptions (tokens/$, caching/batching)

Jordan — thanks for the quick sync earlier. As we discussed, attaching a focused draft that isolates the unit economics assumptions we'll need to lock in during the MAP so we can sign off on POC scope and runway. Key asks up front:
- Can you share a short representative sample of typical request length and the percent of calls that hit a short-context path (<128 tokens)? (we've attached token-profile.csv for you to populate)
- Confirm acceptable latency SLO during the POC (our default target is p95 < 400ms for single-turn generation)
- Procurement: any constraints on retention/telemetry we should bake into the POC contract?

High level notes from our side (see MAP-draft-v2.pdf):
- Baseline token price: we model $0.0018 per 1k input+output tokens for the selected open model variant (quantized). This is preliminary and sensitive to batching and KV-cache hit rates.
- Caching: For prefix-heavy workloads we expect 20–40% effective token reduction from prefix/KV reuse in steady state; we'll instrument an edge cache plus a small Redis-backed KV cache for the POC.
- Batching: We recommend a conservative batching profile for POC (batch window 20ms, max batch 8) to balance latency and throughput. This usually yields ~1.6x cost savings versus no-batching for mid tail request rates.

Please review the attached and drop numbers in token-profile.csv. Ben — can you confirm the quick SE checklist we'll run to validate caching behavior on day 2 of the POC?

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@stratoshealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, procurement@stratoshealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — baseline cost assumptions (tokens/$, caching/batching)

Thanks Vivek. I populated a quick pass of token-profile.csv and attached to this reply. A few clarifications from our side:
- ~65% of calls are short-context (patient summary retrieval then a 1–2 line assistant reply), ~25% are medium (200–400 tokens total), 10% long (500–1500 tokens).
- Latency SLO: for clinicians the target is p95 < 500ms; for batch back-office jobs p95 < 1.2s is acceptable.
- Retention: procurement flagged that PHI telemetry must be strictly anonymized before we send any logs; they prefer aggregated token counts and sampled traces.

Procurement will join a call after you send the MAP with explicit POC acceptance criteria.

Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Product Lead, StratosHealth
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@stratoshealth.com>
Cc: Alex Moreau <alex@cloudbuy.io>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — baseline cost assumptions (tokens/$, caching/batching)

Jordan — good notes. I ran a quick back-of-envelope based on your distribution and Vivek's baseline token price:
- Weighted tokens per request (approx): 0.65*80 + 0.25*300 + 0.10*1000 = ~197 tokens/request.
- At $0.0018 per 1k tokens that implies ~$0.000355 per request (model-only).
- With expected batching (20ms window, avg batch size ~4) and 30% KV cache hit we conservatively model ~45% reduction in billable tokens across the POC traffic shape. That pushes estimated model unit cost to ~$0.000195 per request.
- Add infra (GPU amortization + network) and telemetry overhead: net unit cost ~ $0.00065–0.0008 per request depending on run-hours and concurrent load.

Validation plan (SE checklist for day 2):
- Instrument token counters and KV hit rate metrics (prometheus)
- Run a 30-minute traffic replay of your medium/long samples and measure p95 latency and batch sizes
- Verify anonymization pipeline for telemetry (see procurement questions)

I've attached a starter PoC traffic workbook (poc-traffic-estimates.xlsx) with the math. Alex from CloudBuy — we're planning to use your managed KV cache for the POC; can you confirm SLA for cache p99 availability?

Ben
Sr. Solutions Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Moreau <alex@cloudbuy.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@stratoshealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 12:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — baseline cost assumptions (tokens/$, caching/batching)

Ben — CloudBuy confirms p99 cache availability SLA of 99.8% for our managed Redis tier during the POC window and can enable data-at-rest encryption and HIPAA-addendum on request. We'll provide a short runbook for connection pooling to avoid cold-start latencies.

Alex Moreau
Partnerships, CloudBuy
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@stratoshealth.com>, procurement@stratoshealth.com, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: MAP milestone + procurement ask: POC acceptance & billing cap

Jordan / Procurement — next steps to lock calendar and procurement items:
- We propose the MAP timeline:
  1) Week 0 (kickoff): finalize token-profile.csv + sign POC SOW
  2) Week 1: SE setup, cache + batching instrumentation, dry run traffic replay
  3) Week 2: Live POC (72h steady-state), collect telemetry and cost report
  4) Week 3: Evaluation window & decision checkpoint (go/iterate/stop)

- Billing cap request: for the POC we can offer a soft cap of $6k for the month with overage alerts and a one-time 10% credit if total model usage exceeds the cap due to unforeseen traffic.
- Procurement: to meet your anonymization needs we will only transmit aggregated token metrics and sampled traces by default. If you need raw logs we can define an on-prem collection step in the SOW.

Please confirm acceptance of the timeline and cap so we can issue an updated SOW (I will attach a redline-friendly DocuSign link once you confirm).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sales, Redwood Inference
